angles.drive: You stay calm under pressure, and it shows. Under pressure you have something solid to hold, so you save your calm for the hard moment rather than the ordinary day. Let the quiet days have some of it, since that calm is yours either way.
angles.cost_self: Whenever pressure comes on, you turn calm and useful. Holding steady for everyone feels better than being held yourself, and that keeps you in a crisis after it needs you. Let one hard week run without you, then take back the rest you give away.
angles.cost_others: Your calm is what you offer first in a crisis. You would rather carry the hard part for someone than watch them shake, so you take it off their hands before their calm gets a chance. Let someone else stay calm beside you for once.

angles.drive: Taking charge is a reflex for you. You would rather own a wrong call than leave one with no owner, and you take charge before anyone asks. Keep taking charge, and let a few calls be someone else's to carry.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a plan stalls, you take charge before checking whether you wanted it. Deciding feels more like safety than like a load to you, so you take on calls that were never yours. Turn one down, and you get back the evenings those calls took.
angles.cost_others: For you, looking after a group means taking charge of it. You would rather hand people an answer than wait while they find one, and the finding is what you take from them. Leave one call open long enough for someone else to make.

angles.drive: Pushing through is how you get to the end of anything hard. You need something to push against, so you finish under strain more easily than at ease. Push on, and notice which jobs you only finish when something pushes back.
angles.cost_self: Under strain, you push through without a second thought. Pushing to the far side feels more honest to you than asking for less, and you never try the lighter road. Make one job easy on purpose, and keep the strength that pushing costs.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you push through, you bring the people with you along at your pace. You would rather hold the pace than slow it for someone, and that costs them the pause you never take yourself. Match the slowest once, and see what gets done anyway.

angles.drive: Being hard on yourself is the one pressure you never question. Your own judge gets there before anyone else's, and you would rather be hard on yourself first than hear it from outside. Do not forget that you set this standard and can lower it.
angles.cost_self: Where a job is done, you are hard on yourself about what could have been better. Judging your own work feels more like control than being judged, so praise never gets in. It is worth remembering that you leave the credit you earned unspent.
angles.cost_others: You stay hard on yourself in front of the people you love. Doing it right matters more to you than being easy company, so each kindness you refuse teaches them to keep theirs. Keep in mind that how you treat yourself reaches them too.

angles.drive: You are never off duty, even when nothing needs guarding. Standing down feels like losing rank rather than taking a rest, so you keep watch over quiet weeks as closely as hard ones. Remember that you are allowed to let a quiet week pass unguarded.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the work ends, you find a reason to stay on duty. Being needed feels more solid than being free, so a day off turns into waiting for a call. You would do well to remember that the rest you refuse does not wait.
angles.cost_others: You come home on duty, and your family gets the guard rather than the person. Keeping watch feels more useful than being there, so your attention stays on the next problem. You were wanted off duty more than on it, and that is worth remembering.

angles.drive: You shut people out before they get close enough to press on you. Your own pressure is plenty, so shutting out anyone else's feels like safety rather than loss. Try to remember that shutting out the pressure shuts out the closeness with it.
angles.cost_self: Where help is offered, you shut it out kindly. Being pressed by no one suits you better than being helped, so you carry what was meant for two. It is worth keeping in mind that you pay alone for each hand you refuse.
angles.cost_others: Reaching for you is pressure too, so you shut out the people who try. Being alone matters more than being understood, and you shut the door hardest on the ones closest. What you should remember is that you leave them outside without a reason.

angles.drive: Staying calm under pressure is load-bearing structure for you, and everyone leaning on it can tell. Deadlines collapse, clients raise their voices, and yours holds the level it keeps on an easy Tuesday. People bring you their panic the way they bring valuables to a vault.
angles.cost_self: The launch broke at nine and the group chat caught fire. Your first message, posted at 9:04, was a numbered list. By the third number the chat had gone quiet and gone to work, and the fire was just weather again.
angles.cost_others: New teammates think you are unbothered, and older ones know better. The calm is built, wall by wall, and it holds because you decided long ago that panicking is a second emergency. Nobody has seen the construction. They just live inside it.

angles.drive: Taking charge comes to you the way gravity comes to heavy things, without asking. In any group without a plan, the plan starts collecting around you. You rarely raise your voice. The instructions simply sound like the ground everyone was waiting to stand on.
angles.cost_self: The building alarm went off mid-meeting, and within a minute the whole floor was following your voice to the stairwell. Nobody elected you. By the time everyone stood outside counting heads, it seemed obvious that they always would have.
angles.cost_others: People obey your stillness more than they obey other people’s shouting. Committees route hard calls to you without formally deciding to, and visitors assume you hold a title two levels above the one on your door. The assumption does your paperwork for you.

angles.drive: Outlasting is your actual weapon, and you know exactly how long you can hold. Pressure campaigns, difficult vendors, slow disputes: your position is stocked for winters other people never planned for. You do not need to win quickly. You need to still be there.
angles.cost_self: The negotiation dragged into its fourth month, and the other side started making mistakes born of impatience. You had scheduled your patience in advance, supplies and all. The terms you signed in month five were the ones you wrote in week one.
angles.cost_others: Rivals who try to rattle you end their campaigns tired and on schedule. Colleagues have watched vendors, auditors, and one memorable landlord take a run at your position and slide off it. Waiting you out has been tried many times. It has not once worked.

angles.drive: Defenses are your first architecture, and by now they go up before anything has attacked. New ideas, new people, new plans all get met at the gate and asked for papers. The walls keep trouble out. They keep a good deal else out with it.
angles.cost_self: The proposal died in your inbox behind three clarifying questions and a request for precedent. It was a good proposal. The author knew better than to push, which is exactly how the last four good proposals ended, quietly, at the wall.
angles.cost_others: People pitch to you the way they approach a fortified city, with supplies, patience, and low expectations. Half of them no longer bother. What feels like standards from inside the walls looks, from the road, like a gate that stopped opening years ago.

angles.drive: Force is your default tool, even for jobs that needed a lighter one. The email that required one sentence got a policy. The teenager who needed a talk got a lockdown. Every response lands heavier than the problem, and the problem learns to hide instead of heal.
angles.cost_self: Someone missed one deadline, and by Friday there was a tracking sheet, a check-in meeting, and a new rule with their situation’s shape pressed into it. The sheet outlived the problem by a year. Everyone still fills it in, quietly resenting its birthday.
angles.cost_others: People stopped bringing you small problems, because your solutions never come in small. They handle things quietly and tell you afterward, or never. It reads to you as being kept out of the loop. It reads to them as keeping the peace affordable.

angles.drive: Pressing on is your answer to almost everything, including the things that needed releasing instead. The project grinds, the argument grinds, the schedule grinds, and your grip never loosens on its own. Endurance this strong has forgotten that stopping is also a decision.
angles.cost_self: Year three of the side business that broke even in year one and never grew. Every Sunday night, the same four hours go in. You have stopped asking whether it works. The work itself became the answer, and the question quietly left.
angles.cost_others: People admire your persistence first, then worry about it. From nearby, the grind stopped looking like ambition somewhere along the way and started looking like a stone you cannot put down. Friends have begun asking, gently, what would happen if you just set it there.
